title: Simplified AsyncIterator ↔ ReadableStream ergonomics proposal and migration kit
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Background: Teams building on the TypeScript SDK keep running into subtle ergonomics issues when integrating streaming responses with DOM/Node Web Streams and consumer-facing async iteration. Existing examples in our repo show many ad-hoc adapters which cause duplicate error-handling, inconsistent cancellation semantics, and surprising backpressure behavior. Goal: propose a small, well-documented surface that makes it easy to convert between AsyncIterator/AsyncIterable and ReadableStream in a predictable way, provide migration helpers, and add tests/examples that reduce customer bugs and support load.

Scope and non-goals: This ticket focuses on the SDK surface and lightweight helpers (no runtime changes). We will not ship a new transport; instead we provide adapters and ergonomic wrappers. Follow-up work can optimize kernel-level batching or runtime streaming behavior if needed.

Proposed API: Add two top-level helpers exported from @redwood/sdk/streams: 
- toReadableStream<T>(iter: AsyncIterable<T>): ReadableStream<T> 
- fromReadableStream<T>(stream: ReadableStream<T>): AsyncIterable<T>
- small utility: pipelineWithAbort(signal, ...streams) for common patterns (string/byte framing is out-of-scope).

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Use Web Streams semantics for backpressure in browsers and node (node 18+ native ReadableStream).
- Cancellation mapping: when the ReadableStream is canceled, underlying iterator.return() will be called if available. If iterator throws, the stream will be errored. This matches most user expectations but means adapters need to forward errors in both directions.
- Avoid heavy abstractions (no observable/event-emitter) to keep surface minimal and easy to audit for security.

Examples (user-facing snippets):
1) Consume a streaming completion as ReadableStream in browser code:
const responseIter = sdk.chat.streamCompletion({ prompt });
const rs = toReadableStream(responseIter);
// pipe to an HTML element
const rsReader = rs.getReader();
// read loop omitted for brevity (see docs)

2) Feed a browser ReadableStream into SDK helper that expects async iteration:
const clientStream = fromReadableStream(document.getElementById('file-input').stream());
for await (const chunk of clientStream) {
  await sdk.uploadChunk({ chunk });
}

Migration kit: include a small codemod and a recipe doc (Confluence) with mapping table from older helpers we found in repo to the new helpers. Provide examples for: cancel propagation, error handling, and resuming after transient errors (retry guidance).

Testing and QA: Add unit tests that validate: backpressure propagation, cancellation maps to iterator.return(), error surface equivalence, and cross-environment compatibility (Node 18, Cloud Worker, Chromium-based browsers). Add a small e2e example in packages/examples/streaming-adapter showcasing a chat widget using toReadableStream.

Rollout plan: 
- Week 1: Merge prototype helpers behind feature flag (sdk.streams.beta).
- Week 2: Land docs + examples + codemod.
- Week 3: Collection of internal migration PRs for our top 8 integrations.
- Week 4: Flip default and remove flag if metrics look good.

Metrics and success criteria: reduce internal support tickets mentioning "stream error" or "cancellation" by 50% for new SDK users; measure adoption by number of packages consuming toReadableStream/fromReadableStream in our monorepo; no increase in telemetry errors for streaming endpoints.

Open questions / discussion items for review: 
- Do we need a framing codec in the helpers (text vs bytes)? I recommend leaving framing to caller.
- Should we expose a debug hook for tracing chunk timings? (opt-in only)

Links and artifacts: design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SDK/pages/TS+Stream+Ergonomics (DRAFT); PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1297; internal examples: packages/examples/streaming-adapter (WIP).
